findings.text: Retry entrypoint provides deferred initialization: when a global retry permission flag is set it queues global detector work, otherwise it does nothing. Caller contract requires invocation before late initialization phase.
Late check entrypoint finalizes retry handling by clearing retry permission, draining any queued detector work to quiescence, initializing watchdog sysctl controls, and reporting success.

Main detector initialization notes default behavior on full nohz systems, initializes the watchdog CPU set from the timer housekeeping set, probes hardlockup support, records availability or enables later retry on probe failure, then performs detector setup.

Retry permission lifecycle has three states: set on hardlockup probe failure during init, tested by retry entrypoint to decide whether to queue work, and permanently cleared by late check before flushing work.
Buddy hardlockup probe establishes a miss threshold of three sampling periods and always reports success to its caller.

Buddy enable prepares a newly online CPU by refreshing its own watchdog timestamp and the successor CPU timestamp, orders those refreshes before membership publication, then adds the CPU to the buddy mask.
Buddy disable prepares for CPU removal by refreshing the successor CPU timestamp when valid, orders that refresh before membership removal, then removes the departing CPU from the buddy mask.

Buddy membership updates require a write barrier between timestamp refresh and mask mutation so remote checkers either observe refreshed state or unchanged membership; enable and disable each pair with the buddy checker as counterpart.
Buddy layer keeps one file scoped CPU mask recording which CPUs participate in mutual hardlockup checking.

Perf layer state comprises a per CPU event pointer, a per CPU monotonic timestamp, a per CPU rearm counter, a read mostly sampling threshold, and a global atomic count of CPUs with an active watchdog event.

Timestamp filtered builds accept an overflow only when elapsed monotonic time since the per CPU timestamp reaches a global threshold; short deltas are rejected up to a bounded number of consecutive rejections, after which acceptance is forced and timestamp plus counter reset. Unfiltered builds always accept and initialization is a no operation.

Perf overflow handler first neutralizes event throttling state, then ignores work during panic or when timestamp filtering rejects the sample, otherwise forwards the current CPU and register context to the hardlockup checker.

Event creation derives a sample period from the global watchdog threshold, attempts creation with primary hardware attributes on the requested CPU with the overflow callback, and on error retries once with fallback attributes before returning either event or error.

Perf enable must execute on the target CPU, creates the detector event and quietly returns on failure, increments the active CPU count with an informational message on first enable, warns on preexisting per CPU event leakage, stores the new event, initializes timestamp state, then enables counting.
Perf disable must execute on the target CPU and, when a per CPU event exists, disables it, releases it, clears the per CPU slot, and decrements the active CPU count.

Period adjustment is inert unless hardlockup detection is enabled and a per CPU event exists; it also returns when the requested period already matches, otherwise it requests an event period change and reports failure.
Perf stop and restart paths assert that CPUs are held for write and then iterate over online CPUs to disable or enable each existing per CPU event.

Perf stop unconditionally disables every existing online CPU event during early initialization. Restart additionally checks the global enabled flag first and does nothing when hardlockup support is not enabled.

Architecture availability defaults to true through a weak symbol. Probe fails when NMI is unavailable or when the derived sample period is zero, fails permanently after logging when a trial event cannot be created, and otherwise releases the trial event and reports success.
Primary and fallback perf attributes both request hardware cycle counting with pinned and initially disabled counters and carry the attribute structure size.

Stale timestamp and membership races can cause false lockup reports around CPU hotplug and checker handoff; the code mitigates them by pre refreshing checked CPUs and by barrier ordered mask publication. Perf timestamp filtering also bounds consecutive filtered samples to avoid permanent suppression on coarse clocks.

CPU affinity violations during perf enable or disable and leakage of a prior per CPU event are treated as programming errors and emit one time warnings without correcting the underlying state beyond normal handling.
